title: What does PermissionedDomainSet do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of PermissionedDomainSet and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, PermissionedDomainSet creates or updates a credential-based permissioned domain. [1]

AcceptedCredentials defines which issuer and credential-type combinations can qualify an account. The domain's owner chooses these conditions; the ledger checks the specified credentials rather than performing independent KYC. Check acceptance, expiration and issuer trust. Membership is a scoped ledger permission, not a blanket regulatory license or a statement that every member is safe to trade with. [1]

The PermissionedDomainSet reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using PermissionedDomainSet, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
